1.why: verify-token requires token.sessionId === session.id and accountBinding match before accepting the reset token.

2.why: Tokens are bound to sessionId, so the same reset code is rejected for a different session/user.

3.why: set-password does not invalidate or expire other existing sessions after a password change.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key so HTTPS is used, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords via Bun bcrypt; appropriate protection though hashing not encryption.

6.why: No real email body is built with user PII; responses use a generic message that does not disclose private account data.

7.why: Inputs are type/length-checked (validShortString), tokens regex-validated, and passwords run through passwordPolicy.

8.why: testLink is a same-origin path (/?token=...) and client views are restricted to an allowlist with no open redirect.

9.why: There are no email templates that interpolate user input; HTML is a fixed PAGE constant only.

10.why: API returns testToken/testLink/mfaTestCode and the UI logs panel prints recovery tokens and MFA codes.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, but the MFA secret 482913 is hardcoded in the source.

12.why: No default username/password credentials or built-in default login account are defined or accepted.

13.why: limitStatus/recordFailure lock categories after repeated failures (e.g. 5 attempts) for LOCK_MS.

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same generic message whether or not the contact is valid.

15.why: Reset tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes), are long/complex, and bound to the session.
